inlets.label: value
inlets.range: one or more atoms, each at most 64 characters

inlets.doc: Sets the window size. A float is truncated; values outside 1-256 are refused.
inlets.label: size

inlets.doc: Accepts the bound array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so the array's reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: array reference

.array.stream.name: .array.stream

outlets.doc: The array's reference "array <name>" after each message, but only when the window is full. Sent after outlet 1. Nothing is sent when the object has no name.
outlets.label: reference

outlets.doc: How many more values the window needs before it is full; 0 when it is full. Sent after every value or bang.
outlets.label: shortfall

params.doc: Name of the array to fill: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private array.
params.name: name

params.doc: The window size: how many of the latest values the array keeps. Without one, everything is refused until a size arrives on the middle inlet.
params.name: size

.array.sub.description: Outputs a range of elements of a named array, both ends included; with the end before the start, the range is sent in reverse. The same object as .array.subarray.

inlets.doc: Bang, or the bound array's reference "array <name>": send the elements in the range.
inlets.label: trigger

inlets.doc: Sets the first position of the range. A float is truncated; a negative value is refused.
inlets.label: start

inlets.doc: Sets the last position of the range, which is included. Past the end of the array means the end; before the start sends the range reversed. A float is truncated; a negative value is refused.
inlets.label: end

inlets.doc: Accepts the bound array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so the array's reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: array reference

.array.sub.name: .array.sub

outlets.doc: The elements from start to end, both included, as one list; reversed when the end is before the start. A single element leaves as an int, float or symbol.
outlets.label: piece

outlets.doc: Bang when the range holds no elements, for example when the array is empty or the start is past its end.
outlets.label: empty

params.doc: Name of the array to read: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: name

params.doc: The first position of the range before one arrives on the start inlet.
params.name: start

params.doc: The last position of the range (included). Empty, or past the end of the array, means the end. Before the start sends the range reversed.
params.name: end

.array.subarray.description: Outputs a range of elements of a named array, both ends included; with the end before the start, the range is sent in reverse. The same object as .array.sub.

inlets.doc: Bang, or the bound array's reference "array <name>": send the elements in the range.
inlets.label: trigger

inlets.doc: Sets the first position of the range. A float is truncated; a negative value is refused.
inlets.label: start

inlets.doc: Sets the last position of the range, which is included. Past the end of the array means the end; before the start sends the range reversed. A float is truncated; a negative value is refused.
inlets.label: end

inlets.doc: Accepts the bound array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so the array's reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: array reference

.array.subarray.name: .array.subarray

outlets.doc: The elements from start to end, both included, as one list; reversed when the end is before the start. A single element leaves as an int, float or symbol.
outlets.label: piece

outlets.doc: Bang when the range holds no elements, for example when the array is empty or the start is past its end.
outlets.label: empty

params.doc: Name of the array to read: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: name

params.doc: The first position of the range before one arrives on the start inlet.
params.name: start

params.doc: The last position of the range (included). Empty, or past the end of the array, means the end. Before the start sends the range reversed.
params.name: end

.array.thin.description: Removes elements of a named array that repeat the element kept before them. With a tolerance, numbers that close to it count as repeats too, which thins out a stream of values that barely change.

inlets.doc: Bang, or the bound array's reference "array <name>": thin the array now.
inlets.label: trigger

inlets.doc: Sets the largest difference between two numbers that still counts as a repeat. 0 means exact repeats only. Negative values are refused.
inlets.label: tolerance

inlets.doc: Accepts the bound array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so the array's reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: array reference

.array.thin.name: .array.thin

outlets.doc: The array's reference "array <name>" after each thin, so further .array objects can be chained. Sent after outlet 1. Nothing is sent when the object has no name.
outlets.label: reference

outlets.doc: How many elements were removed; 0 when none. Sent before the reference.
outlets.label: removed

params.doc: Name of the array to thin: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: name

params.doc: The largest difference between two numbers that still counts as a repeat. 0 means exact repeats only.
params.name: tolerance

.array.tolist.description: Outputs all elements of a named array as one list. An array of one element sends that element as a single int, float or symbol.

inlets.doc: Bang, or the bound array's reference "array <name>": send the converted array.
inlets.label: trigger

inlets.doc: Accepts the bound array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so the array's reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: array reference

.array.tolist.name: .array.tolist

outlets.doc: The elements in order, as a list; a single element leaves as an int, float or symbol. Items past what a list can hold are dropped.
outlets.label: list

outlets.doc: Bang when the array is empty.
outlets.label: empty

params.doc: Name of the array to use: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: name

.array.tostring.description: Outputs all elements of a named array as one text message, separated by spaces. Unlike .array.tolist, a single number is sent as text, ready for objects that work on text.

inlets.doc: Bang, or the bound array's reference "array <name>": send the converted array.
inlets.label: trigger

inlets.doc: Accepts the bound array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so the array's reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: array reference

.array.tostring.name: .array.tostring

outlets.doc: The elements in order, separated by spaces, always as text. Items past what a list can hold are dropped.
outlets.label: string

outlets.doc: Bang when the array is empty.
outlets.label: empty

params.doc: Name of the array to use: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: name

.array.tosymbol.description: Joins all elements of a named array, without spaces, into one symbol: kick and .wav become kick.wav. The result is always a symbol, even when it looks like a number.

inlets.doc: Bang, or the bound array's reference "array <name>": send the converted array.
inlets.label: trigger

inlets.doc: Accepts the bound array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so the array's reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: array reference

.array.tosymbol.name: .array.tosymbol

outlets.doc: The elements joined into one word, always a symbol. Nothing is sent when the array is too long to fit in one message.
outlets.label: symbol

outlets.doc: Bang when the array is empty.
outlets.label: empty

params.doc: Name of the array to use: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: name

.array.tuplewise.description: Combines two named arrays position by position with an expression, such as $f1 + $f2, and outputs the results as one list. The result is as long as the shorter array.

inlets.doc: Bang, or the left array's reference "array <name>": combine the two arrays. Refused when the expression is missing or did not compile.
inlets.label: trigger

inlets.doc: Accepts the right array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so its reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: right reference

.array.tuplewise.name: .array.tuplewise

outlets.doc: One result per position, as a list. Where either element is a word, the left element is passed through. A single result leaves as an int, float or symbol.
outlets.label: combined

outlets.doc: Bang when either array is empty.
outlets.label: empty

params.doc: Name of the left array: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: left

params.doc: Name of the right array, found the same way. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: right

params.doc: The expression: the rest of the arguments, in .expr syntax. $f1 or $i1 is the left element, $f2 or $i2 the right element and $f3 or $i3 their position. A malformed expression is logged and the object then does nothing.
params.name: expression

.array.union.description: Outputs the elements held by either of two named arrays, each once, as one list. Neither array is changed.

inlets.doc: Bang, or the left array's reference "array <name>": send the result.
inlets.label: trigger

inlets.doc: Accepts the right array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so its reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: right reference

.array.union.name: .array.union

outlets.doc: The left array's elements, then the right array's elements the left does not hold, each once. A single element leaves as an int, float or symbol.
outlets.label: union

outlets.doc: Bang when both arrays are empty.
outlets.label: empty

params.doc: Name of the left array: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: left

params.doc: Name of the right array, found the same way. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: right

.array.unique.description: Outputs the elements of a named array with repeats removed, each at its first occurrence. The array itself is not changed.

inlets.doc: Bang, or the bound array's reference "array <name>": send the array without repeats.
inlets.label: trigger

inlets.doc: Accepts the bound array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so the array's reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: array reference

.array.unique.name: .array.unique

outlets.doc: Each distinct element once, in order of first appearance. A single element leaves as an int, float or symbol.
outlets.label: unique

outlets.doc: Bang when the array is empty.
outlets.label: empty

params.doc: Name of the array to use: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: name

.array.unshift.description: Inserts a value or a list at the front of a named array, moving the other elements up, then sends the array's reference.

inlets.doc: An int, float, word or list to insert at the front. A list keeps its order and is inserted whole, or refused whole when the array cannot take all of it.
inlets.label: element

inlets.doc: Accepts the bound array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so the array's reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: array reference

.array.unshift.name: .array.unshift

outlets.doc: The array's reference "array <name>" after each change, so further .array objects can be chained. Nothing is sent when the object has no name.
outlets.label: reference

params.doc: Name of the array to use: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: name

.array.wrap.description: Outputs the element at a position in a named array, wrapping around: positions past the end start again at the beginning, and -1 is the last element.

inlets.doc: An int fetches the element at that position, wrapped around the array's length, and remembers the position; a bang fetches at the remembered position, and so does the bound array's reference. A list of positions fetches them all at once. A float is truncated.
inlets.label: index

inlets.doc: Accepts the bound array's reference "array <name>" and ignores it, so the array's reference outlet can be wired here. Anything else is refused.
inlets.label: array reference

.array.wrap.name: .array.wrap

outlets.doc: The element, as an int, float or symbol by its spelling. A list of positions gives one list, in the order asked.
outlets.label: element

outlets.doc: Bang when the array is empty, so there is nothing to wrap onto. One bang for a list of positions.
outlets.label: empty

params.doc: Name of the array to use: the .array with this name in the same patcher. Empty uses a private, empty array.
params.name: name

params.doc: The position a bang fetches before any position arrives. Any int; -1 is the last element.
params.name: index

.asin.description: Sends the arc-sine of a number, in radians. Numbers outside -1 to 1 send 0.

inlets.doc: Number; sends the result. Numbers outside -1 to 1 send 0.
inlets.label: in

.asin.name: .asin

outlets.doc: The arc-sine of the input, in radians.
outlets.label: out

.asinh.description: Sends the hyperbolic arc-sine of a number.

inlets.doc: Number; sends the result.
inlets.label: in

.asinh.name: .asinh

outlets.doc: The hyperbolic arc-sine of the input.
outlets.label: out

.atan.description: Sends the arc-tangent of a number, in radians. Use .atan2 for an angle around the full circle.

inlets.doc: Number; sends the result.
inlets.label: in

.atan.name: .atan

outlets.doc: The arc-tangent of the input, in radians.
outlets.label: out

.atan2.description: Sends the angle of the point (x, y) in radians, measured from the positive x axis, from -pi to pi. The left inlet takes y and the right inlet x.

inlets.doc: y coordinate; sends the result.
inlets.label: y

inlets.doc: x coordinate, stored for the next result.
inlets.label: x

.atan2.name: .atan2

outlets.doc: The angle of (x, y) in radians.
outlets.label: out

params.name: x

.atanh.description: Sends the hyperbolic arc-tangent of a number. Numbers at or beyond -1 and 1 send 0.

inlets.doc: Number; sends the result. Numbers at or beyond -1 and 1 send 0.
inlets.label: in

.atanh.name: .atanh

outlets.doc: The hyperbolic arc-tangent of the input.
outlets.label: out

.atodb.description: Converts a linear amplitude to decibels on the engine's scale, where an amplitude of 1 is 100 dB and nothing goes below 0 dB. Subtract 100 for decibels relative to full scale.

inlets.doc: Linear amplitude; sends the result. 0 and below send 0.
inlets.label: in

.atodb.name: .atodb

outlets.doc: The amplitude in decibels; 100 dB is an amplitude of 1.
outlets.label: out

.atoi.description: Converts a message into the character codes of its text and holds them: 'hi' gives 104 105. A bang sends the held codes again, and the other two inlets add to them or replace them without sending.

inlets.doc: The message to convert. It replaces the stored codes and the codes are sent. A bang sends the stored codes again. An empty message clears them and sends nothing.
inlets.label: in

inlets.doc: Adds the codes of the message to the stored codes and sends nothing. Characters are added with no space between messages: 'a' then 'b' gives 97 98.
inlets.label: append

inlets.doc: Replaces the stored codes with the codes of the message and sends nothing. An empty message clears them.
inlets.label: set

.atoi.name: .atoi

outlets.doc: The stored codes as one list, in the order the characters appear: 'hi' leaves as 104 105.
outlets.label: out

.b.description: A button. Any bang or number sends a bang and lights the button until the host next reads it.

inlets.doc: A bang, int or float presses the button.
inlets.label: trigger

.b.name: .b

outlets.doc: A bang for every press.
outlets.label: out

.bag.description: Holds a collection of numbers that a patch adds to and removes from, such as the notes currently held down. A bang sends every number, newest first.

inlets.doc: A number to add or remove, depending on the flag. Also bang, '<value> <flag>', 'cut', 'length', 'clear' and 'send <name>'.
inlets.label: value

inlets.doc: Non-zero: numbers on the left inlet are added. 0: they are removed. Starts at 0.
inlets.label: flag

.bag.name: .bag

outlets.doc: Stored numbers, on bang or 'cut', and the count on 'length'.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: Any argument lets the same number be stored more than once. Without one, each number is held at most once.
params.name: duplicates

.bangbang.description: Sends a bang out every outlet, right to left, whatever arrives. Each outlet's branch finishes before the next outlet fires, so it orders 'do this, then that'.

inlets.doc: Bang, int, float or list. The value is ignored.
inlets.label: in

.bangbang.name: .bangbang

outlets.doc: A bang. The last outlet fires first, outlet 0 last.
outlets.label: out0

outlets.doc: A bang. The last outlet fires first, outlet 0 last.
outlets.label: out1

params.name: outlets

.bendin.description: MIDI pitch-bend input at 7-bit resolution: reports the pitch wheel as 0-127 with 64 at rest. .xbendin reports the full 14 bits.
.bendin.name: .bendin

outlets.doc: The wheel position: 0 fully down, 64 at rest, 127 fully up.
outlets.label: bend

outlets.doc: The channel the message arrived on, 1-16. Sent before the outlets to its left.
outlets.label: channel

params.doc: MIDI input port to listen to, counted from 0; .midiinfo lists them. A port that cannot be opened leaves the object silent, and the patch still loads.
params.name: port

params.doc: MIDI channel to listen to, 1-16, or 0 for all channels. Any other value means all channels. The channel outlet stays either way.
params.name: channel

.bendout.description: Builds a 7-bit MIDI pitch-bend message for .midiout: 0-127 with 64 at rest. .xbendout sends the full 14 bits.

inlets.doc: Pitch bend, 64 at rest; sends the message.
inlets.label: bend

.bendout.name: .bendout

outlets.doc: The pitch-bend message, for .midiout. The fine byte is 0.
outlets.label: midi

params.doc: MIDI channel, counted from 0: 0 is channel 1.
params.name: channel

.bline.description: Ramps a number to a target one step per bang, so whatever bangs it sets the pace. A list of target/count pairs makes a ramp of several segments; the right outlet bangs when the last target is reached.

inlets.doc: A bang sends the next step. A target, '<target> <bangs>', or target/bangs pairs set the ramp. 'stop' and 'set <value>' control it.
inlets.label: in

.bline.name: .bline

outlets.doc: The ramp, one value per bang, ending exactly on the target. An int or a float, as on .line.
outlets.label: out

outlets.doc: A bang when the last target is reached. A ramp cut short by 'stop' sends none.
outlets.label: done

params.doc: The starting value. Written as a float ('0.') it makes the object send floats.
params.name: initial

.bondo.description: Holds one value per inlet and sends all of them, right to left, whenever any inlet receives one. Keeps a set of related values together, so nothing downstream sees half an update.

inlets.doc: Stores a value here and sends every outlet. A bang sends without storing; 'set <message>' stores without sending.
inlets.label: in0

inlets.doc: Stores a value here and sends every outlet. A bang sends without storing; 'set <message>' stores without sending.
inlets.label: in1

.bondo.name: .bondo

outlets.doc: What the matching inlet holds: 0 until it receives something.
outlets.label: out1

params.name: ports

.borax.description: Reports statistics about a stream of notes: serial number, voice, how many notes are sounding, durations and the time between attacks.

inlets.label: pitch

inlets.doc: Velocity for the pitches that follow; sends nothing. 0 means a note-off. Not clamped.
inlets.label: velocity

inlets.doc: A bang reports a note-off for every sounding note, then sets every counter back to 0.
inlets.label: reset

.borax.name: .borax

outlets.doc: The note's number, counting note-ons from 1. The same at its note-on and its note-off. Sent last.
outlets.label: serial

outlets.doc: The voice the note took: the lowest free number, from 1.
outlets.label: voice

outlets.doc: How many notes are sounding, on every note-on and note-off.
outlets.label: poly

outlets.doc: The pitch of the note that started or ended.
outlets.label: pitch

outlets.doc: The stored velocity at a note-on, 0 at a note-off.
outlets.label: velocity

outlets.doc: How many notes have ended, sent at each note-off.
outlets.label: notesoff

outlets.doc: How long the note that just ended lasted, in milliseconds.
outlets.label: duration

outlets.doc: How many delta times have been reported, sent with each one.
outlets.label: deltacount

outlets.doc: Milliseconds since the previous note-on, sent at each note-on after the first and on "delta".
outlets.label: delta

.bucket.description: A shift register for numbers. Each number pushes the stored values one outlet along and every outlet sends what it holds, each one a step older than the outlet to its left.

inlets.doc: A number shifts the register and every outlet sends. A bang sends without shifting. A list of numbers is fed in one number at a time. Also takes 'set <n>', 'clear', 'freeze', 'thaw', 'L2R', 'R2L' and 'roll'.
inlets.label: in

.bucket.name: .bucket

outlets.label: out0

params.name: outlets

.buddy.description: Waits until every inlet has received a value, then sends them all at once, right to left, and starts waiting again. Use it to assemble one event from parts that arrive separately.

inlets.doc: Stores a value here; once every inlet holds one, all are sent. A bang stores 0. On inlet 0, 'clear' empties every inlet.
inlets.label: in1

.buddy.name: .buddy

outlets.label: out0

outlets.doc: What the matching inlet received, sent once the set is complete.
outlets.label: out1

params.name: inlets

.capture.description: Records every value that reaches it, in arrival order, so a patch can be run and then asked what went past. When full, the oldest item makes room for the newest.

.capture.name: .capture

.channelpressure.name: .channelpressure

outlets.label: midi

params.doc: MIDI channel, counted from 0: 0 is channel 1.
params.name: channel

.clip.description: Limits a number to the range low to high and sends it as a float. A number inside the range passes unchanged; any other becomes the nearest limit.

inlets.label: value

inlets.label: low

inlets.doc: Upper limit, stored for the next result.
inlets.label: high

.clip.name: .clip

.clocker.description: While running, sends the time since it was started, in milliseconds, every interval (5 ms by default). With a clock bound, a second outlet sends the beats that clock has moved in the same time.

inlets.label: interval

outlets.doc: The inlet's number plus the offset, followed by the message as it arrived.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: How many inlets to build. A second number is the offset added to every inlet's number, so inlet 0 sends that value.
params.name: inlets

.gate.description: Passes messages from its right inlet out one of its outlets, chosen by a number in the left inlet. Outlets count from 1; 0 closes the gate.

inlets.doc: The outlet to send to, counting from 1. 0 (the start value) or a number with no outlet closes the gate.
inlets.label: select

inlets.doc: Bang, int, float or list to pass to the selected outlet.
inlets.label: in

.gate.name: .gate

outlets.doc: Sends the message when select is 1.
outlets.label: out0

outlets.doc: Sends the message when select is 2.
outlets.label: out1

params.doc: How many outlets to build. Fewer than 2 still builds 2.
params.name: numOutlets

.histo.description: Counts how often each number arrives and sends '<number> <count>' each time. The right inlet reports a number's count without counting it.

inlets.doc: Number: count it and send its count. Bang: send the count of the last counted number again. 'clear': set every count to 0. 'dump': send every number counted so far.
inlets.label: in

inlets.doc: Number: send its count without counting it.
inlets.label: query

.histo.name: .histo

outlets.doc: '<number> <count>': how often this number has been counted.
outlets.label: count

outlets.doc: Bang when a number is outside 0 to size-1; it is not counted.
outlets.label: reject

params.doc: How many numbers can be counted: 0 to size-1. Clamped to 1-4096.
params.name: size

.i.description: An integer number box. A number on the left inlet stores it and sends it, a bang sends it again, and the right inlet stores a number without sending it. Floats are truncated.

inlets.doc: A number sets the value and sends it; a bang sends it again. Also takes its GUI value back, as a one-number list or 'set 0 <value>'.
inlets.label: set/bang

inlets.doc: Stores a number without sending it.
inlets.label: silent set

.i.name: .i

outlets.doc: The value.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: The value the box starts with.
params.name: value

.if.description: Tests a condition and sends one message when it is true and, optionally, another when it is false: '$i1 > 64 then bang else out2 $i1'. The condition and the message items use the .expr language.

inlets.doc: Value for $i1 / $f1; stores it and evaluates. A bang evaluates with the stored values; a list fills the inlets from the left, then evaluates.

.if.name: .if

outlets.doc: The then or else message, unless it starts with out2. One item is sent as an int or float, several as a list, 'bang' as a bang.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: <condition> then <message> [else <message>], e.g. '$i1 > 64 then bang else out2 $i1'.
params.name: statement

.incdec.description: A stepper over a whole number. 'inc' and 'dec', or a signed step count on the middle inlet, move the value inside a range that clamps or wraps; a number sets it without sending and a bang sends it.

inlets.doc: A bang sends the value without moving it. A number, or 'set <n>', sets it without sending. 'inc' and 'dec' move one step up or down and send. Also takes its GUI value back, as a one-number list or 'set 0 <value>'.
inlets.label: value

inlets.doc: An int n moves n steps (negative moves down) and sends the result; 0 just sends the value. A float is truncated.
inlets.label: nudge

inlets.doc: Sets the step size. A negative step makes 'inc' go down. A float is truncated.
inlets.label: step

.incdec.name: .incdec

outlets.doc: The value, whenever it moves or is read.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: How far one step moves the value; a negative step reverses 'inc' and 'dec'.
params.name: step

params.doc: The bottom of the range.
params.name: minimum

params.doc: The top of the range.
params.name: maximum

params.doc: 0 stops at the ends of the range; 1 wraps around to the other end.
params.name: wrap

.inlet.description: A message inlet of the subpatcher it is in. With index N, whatever the parent sends to the subpatcher's inlet N comes out of this object, inside the subpatcher.

inlets.doc: Receives what the parent patch sends to the subpatcher's inlet with this index. A cord connected to that inlet lands here. Bang, int, float and list.
inlets.label: from parent

.inlet.name: .inlet

outlets.doc: The incoming message, unchanged, inside the subpatcher. An int stays an int, a list a list.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: Which inlet of the enclosing subpatcher this object is, shared with ~inlet. Give every boundary object its own number.
params.name: index

.iter.description: Sends the items of a list out one at a time, first to last, so objects that take single numbers can process each one. A bang sends the last list again.

inlets.doc: The list to send item by item. An int or float is a list of one. A bang sends the last list again.
inlets.label: in

.iter.name: .iter

outlets.doc: Each item of the list, first to last, as an int, float or symbol.
outlets.label: out

.itoa.description: Converts character codes into the text they spell and holds it: 104 105 gives 'hi'. A bang sends the held text again, and the other two inlets add to it or replace it without sending. The inverse of .atoi.

inlets.doc: The character codes to convert: an int, a float (truncated) or a list of them. They replace the stored text and the text is sent. A bang sends the stored text again. An empty message clears it and sends nothing.
inlets.label: in

inlets.doc: Adds the characters the codes spell to the stored text and sends nothing. Use it to build a word one character at a time, then bang inlet 0 to send it.
inlets.label: append

inlets.doc: Replaces the stored text with the characters the codes spell and sends nothing. An empty message clears it.
inlets.label: set

.itoa.name: .itoa

outlets.doc: The stored text as a list: 104 105 leaves as 'hi'. Always a list, even when the text reads as a number.
outlets.label: out

.join.description: Joins the messages held by several inlets into one list, end to end. Unlike .pack, each inlet holds a whole message of any length. .unjoin splits a list the other way.

inlets.doc: The first piece of the list. Stores the whole message, whatever its length. Sends the list unless the trigger arguments make this inlet cold. A bang sends without storing; 'set <message>' stores without sending.
inlets.label: in0

inlets.doc: The piece in this position. Stores the whole message, whatever its length. Sends the list only when a trigger argument names this inlet. A bang sends without storing; 'set <message>' stores without sending.
inlets.label: in1

.join.name: .join

outlets.doc: Every inlet's piece, end to end in inlet order. A result of one atom is sent as an int, float or symbol; an empty result sends nothing.
outlets.label: list

params.doc: The number of inlets, each starting out holding 0. Any further arguments name the inlets, counted from 0, that send the list when written; -1 makes every inlet send. Without them only the leftmost inlet sends.
params.name: inlets triggers
params.range: inlets 1-256, then any number of triggers -1 or 0 to inlets-1

.kslider.description: A piano keyboard. A pitch on the left inlet presses that key at the stored velocity and sends velocity and pitch; velocity 0 releases it. The state is the velocity held on each of the 128 keys.

inlets.doc: A pitch presses that key at the stored velocity; '<pitch> <velocity>' plays it at that velocity, and velocity 0 releases it. Also 128 numbers (the whole keyboard), 'set <pitch> <velocity>', 'clear' and bang.
inlets.label: pitch

inlets.doc: The velocity for pitches that arrive after it. Sends nothing. Clamped to 0-127; a float is truncated.
inlets.label: velocity

.kslider.name: .kslider

outlets.doc: The pitch of the key that moved. Sent after the velocity.
outlets.label: pitch

outlets.doc: The key's new velocity: 0 for a release. Sent before the pitch, so it pairs with the pitch in the next object.
outlets.label: velocity

params.doc: The velocity a bare pitch is played at, until the right inlet or a '<pitch> <velocity>' list changes it.
params.name: velocity

.l.description: A list box. A bang sends the stored list; a list arriving on the inlet replaces it without sending it.

inlets.doc: A bang sends the stored list; a list replaces it silently.
inlets.label: trigger/set

.l.name: .l

outlets.doc: The stored list.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: The list the box starts with.
params.name: message

.led.description: A labelled on/off indicator. It latches by default (a number sets it, a bang flips it) or registers presses with the 'momentary' keyword, and sends its state and its label.

inlets.doc: Latching: a number sets the state (0 off, anything else on) and a bang flips it. Momentary: any number or bang is a press. In both modes a one-number list or 'set 0 <value>' sets the state outright. Everything here sends.
inlets.label: state

.led.name: .led

outlets.doc: The state. Sent last.
outlets.label: state

outlets.doc: The label, so a bank of controls wired into one object can say which one fired. Empty when the control has no label. Sent first.
outlets.label: label

params.doc: An optional 'momentary' keyword, then the label. The words of the label are joined with single spaces.
params.name: label

.line.description: Ramps a number to a target over a given time, sending a value every grain (20 ms by default) and a bang from the right outlet on arrival. A list of target/time pairs makes a ramp of several segments.

inlets.doc: A target, '<target> <time> [<grain>]', or target/time pairs. 'stop', 'pause', 'resume' and 'set <value>' control the ramp.
inlets.label: in

inlets.doc: The time in milliseconds the next target takes. It is used by one target only, then goes back to 0.
inlets.label: time

inlets.doc: The time in milliseconds between values. Below 1 it counts as 20. It stays set.
inlets.label: grain

.line.name: .line

outlets.doc: The ramp, one value per grain, ending exactly on the target. An int or a float: see the notes.
outlets.label: out

outlets.doc: A bang when the last target is reached. A ramp cut short by 'stop' sends none.
outlets.label: done

params.doc: The starting value. Written as a float ('0.') it makes the object send floats.
params.name: initial

params.doc: The time in milliseconds between values. Below 1 it counts as 20.
params.name: grain

.linedrive.description: Maps a number onto an exponential curve: inputMax gives outputMax, and each step below it divides the output by the curve. Lets a linear control, such as a MIDI controller, drive a frequency or a gain evenly.

inlets.doc: Number to map; sends the result.
inlets.label: value

inlets.doc: Input that gives outputMax, stored for the next result.
inlets.label: inputMax

inlets.doc: Output at inputMax, stored for the next result.
inlets.label: outputMax

inlets.doc: Curve base, stored for the next result. Larger is steeper; 1 gives a constant outputMax; 0 or below sends 0.
inlets.label: curve

.linedrive.name: .linedrive

outlets.doc: The number mapped onto the curve.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: Input that gives outputMax.
params.name: inputMax

params.doc: Output at inputMax.
params.name: outputMax

params.doc: Curve base. Larger is steeper; 1 gives a constant outputMax.
params.name: curve

.listfunnel.description: Sends each item of a list out as a two-item list: its index, then the item. Use it to address items by position with .route, .sel or .spray.

inlets.doc: The list to number. An int or float is a list of one. 'offset <n>' sets the number given to the first item, without sending anything. Bang is not accepted.
inlets.label: in

.listfunnel.name: .listfunnel

outlets.doc: One two-item list per item, first to last: the item's index, then the item unchanged.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: The index given to the first item. The 'offset' message changes it while the patch runs; that change is not saved.
params.name: offset

.loadbang.description: Sends a bang when the patch it is in has finished loading, so a saved patch can set up its own starting state. A bang at the inlet sends one by hand.

inlets.doc: A bang sends a bang, as a load does. Use it to initialise a patch built with CreateObject.
inlets.label: trigger

.loadbang.name: .loadbang

outlets.doc: A bang when the patch has finished loading, and for each bang in.
outlets.label: out

.loadmess.description: Sends its arguments as a message when the patch it is in has finished loading, such as '.loadmess 0.5' to set a gain. A bang at the inlet sends it by hand.

inlets.doc: A bang sends the stored message, as a load does. 'set <message>' replaces it without sending; a bare 'set' empties it. Other lists are ignored.
inlets.label: trigger/set

.loadmess.name: .loadmess

outlets.doc: The stored message when the patch has finished loading, and for each bang in: a bang, an int, a float or a list, by its form. Nothing when empty.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: The message to send, such as '60' or 'mode 2'. At most 256 characters; with none, the object sends nothing.
params.name: message

.m.description: A message box. A bang sends the stored text as the message it spells: a number, a bang, a list or a command. A message arriving on the inlet replaces the text without sending it.

inlets.doc: A bang sends the stored message; a list or a word message replaces it silently.
inlets.label: trigger/set

.m.name: .m

outlets.doc: The stored message, as the message it spells: one number is an int or a float, the word 'bang' is a bang, a list starting with a number is a list, and text starting with any other word is a command to objects that take one ('stop' to '~line', 'allnotesoff' to '.midiout') and a list to every other object.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: The text the box starts with.
params.name: message

.makenote.description: Plays a note: sends a pitch and velocity now, and the same pitch with velocity 0 after a duration in milliseconds.

inlets.doc: A pitch plays a note with the stored velocity and duration. A list "pitch velocity" sets the velocity first. "stop" releases every sounding note; "clear" forgets them.
inlets.label: pitch

inlets.doc: Velocity for the notes that follow; sends nothing. Clamped to 0-127. With 0, the pair passes through and no release is scheduled.
inlets.label: velocity

inlets.doc: Duration in milliseconds for the notes that follow; sends nothing. A negative value counts as 0. Note values and ticks are not supported.
inlets.label: duration

.makenote.name: .makenote

outlets.doc: The pitch, when the note plays and again when it is released. Sent last.
outlets.label: pitch

outlets.doc: The velocity when the note plays, 0 when it is released.
outlets.label: velocity

params.doc: Starting velocity. With 0, notes pass through and no release is scheduled, so set it or send a velocity before playing.
params.name: velocity

params.doc: Starting duration in milliseconds. 0 releases each note on the next audio block.
params.name: duration

.match.description: Watches a stream of numbers and sends the last few as a list when they match the pattern in its arguments. The word 'nn' matches any number, so '.match 1 nn 3' sends '1 5 3' after 1, 5, 3.

inlets.doc: Int, float or list: each number takes the next place in the stream. Also 'clear' and 'set <pattern>'.
inlets.label: in

.match.name: .match

outlets.doc: The values that matched, in arrival order and spelling, as a list as long as the pattern.
outlets.label: match

params.doc: The sequence to watch for: numbers, matched exactly, and 'nn' for any number. At most 256 elements.
params.name: pattern
params.range: any list of numbers and nn

.matrix.description: Routes messages from its data inlets to its outlets as set by connection messages, like .router, but each connection has a gain that scales the numbers passing through. At a gain of 1 messages pass unchanged.

inlets.doc: Sets the connections: '<inlet> <outlet> <gain>' (gain 0 disconnects), 'connect <inlet> <outlet> [gain]', 'disconnect <inlet> <outlet>', 'clear' and 'dumpconnections'. Inlets and outlets count from 0, starting at the first data inlet.
inlets.label: connections

inlets.doc: A message here goes out every outlet this inlet is connected to, right to left, scaled by each connection's gain.
inlets.label: in0

inlets.doc: A message here goes out every outlet this inlet is connected to, right to left, scaled by each connection's gain.
inlets.label: in1

.matrix.name: .matrix

outlets.doc: Messages from every inlet connected to this outlet, each scaled by its connection's gain. Messages from different inlets are not added together.
outlets.label: out0

outlets.doc: Messages from every inlet connected to this outlet, each scaled by its connection's gain. Messages from different inlets are not added together.
outlets.label: out1

outlets.doc: The answer to 'dumpconnections': one '<inlet> <outlet> <gain>' list per connection.
outlets.label: connections

params.doc: How many data inlets, then how many data outlets (2 each by default), then the gain 'connect' uses when none is given (1 by default).
params.name: inputs

.matrixctrl.description: A grid of cells, columns by rows, such as a step pattern or a routing patchbay. '<column> <row> <value>' sets a cell, and every change is sent in that same form, so the grid can drive .matrix or .router directly.

inlets.doc: '<column> <row> <value>' sets one cell; a list of every cell sets the whole grid; 'set <index> <value>' sets one cell by index; 'clear', 'getrow <row>', 'getcolumn <column>' and bang. Lists and bangs only.
inlets.label: grid

.matrixctrl.name: .matrixctrl

outlets.doc: Changed cells as '<column> <row> <value>': one list per cell, ready for the control inlet of .matrix or .router.
outlets.label: cell

outlets.doc: One row's or one column's values as a list, in answer to 'getrow' or 'getcolumn'.
outlets.label: line

params.doc: The number of columns, then optionally the number of rows (default 8) and the lowest and highest value a cell can hold (default 0 and 1).
params.name: columns
params.range: 1-256, optional rows 1-256, optional minimum, optional maximum

.maximum.description: Sends the larger of a number and a stored value. The right inlet sets the stored value; a list sends its largest item.

inlets.doc: Number: send the larger of it and the stored value. Bang: send the last result again. List: send its largest item, and store the second largest.
inlets.label: in

inlets.doc: Value to compare with, stored without sending.
inlets.label: compare

.maximum.name: .maximum

outlets.doc: The larger of the input and the stored value.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: Starting value to compare with, and what a bang sends before the first result.
params.name: initial

.mean.description: Sends the average of every number received so far, and how many numbers that is. A list sends the average of its own items and starts the average over.

inlets.doc: Number: add it to the average and send. Bang: send the average again. List: average its items, forgetting earlier numbers. 'clear' or 'reset': start over without sending.
inlets.label: in

.mean.name: .mean

outlets.doc: The average; 0 before any number has arrived.
outlets.label: mean
outlets.range: between the smallest and largest input

outlets.doc: How many numbers the average includes. Sent before the average.
outlets.label: count

.metro.description: Sends a bang at a regular interval while it runs, starting with one bang the moment it starts. The interval is in milliseconds (1000 by default) or a beat time on a domain clock.

inlets.doc: A non-zero number or a bang starts the metro (a bang restarts a running one from now); 0 or 'stop' stops it. 'clock <name>' sets the clock for a beat interval.
inlets.label: on/off

inlets.doc: Sets the interval, in milliseconds or as a beat time. A running metro keeps going at the new interval without restarting.
inlets.label: period
inlets.range: 1+ ms, or a note value / tick count

.metro.name: .metro

outlets.doc: A bang on every tick, and one when the metro starts.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: The interval in milliseconds. A change reaches a running metro one tick later.
params.name: period

params.doc: The interval in beats on the bound clock. 0 uses the millisecond interval instead. A plain number in the right inlet sets it back to 0.
params.name: periodbeats

.midiflush.description: Passes a MIDI byte stream through and remembers which notes it left sounding. A bang sends a note-off for each of them.

inlets.doc: MIDI bytes as a list of byte values, a message from a sender object, or one int at a time; all pass through. A bang sends a note-off for every sounding note.
inlets.label: midi

.midiflush.name: .midiflush

outlets.doc: The stream, unchanged, plus the note-offs a bang sends, as lists such as 128 60 0.
outlets.label: midi

.midiformat.description: Builds raw MIDI messages from notes, controllers, program changes, pressure and pitch bend. The inverse of .midiparse; each message leaves as a list of byte values.

inlets.doc: "pitch velocity"; a bare pitch sends velocity 0, a release. Sends a note-on.
inlets.label: note

inlets.doc: Polyphonic key pressure as "pitch pressure"; a bare pitch sends 0.
inlets.label: poly

inlets.doc: Control change as "controller value"; a bare number sends value 0.
inlets.label: control

inlets.doc: Program change, numbered from 1.
inlets.label: program

inlets.doc: Channel pressure: one value for the whole channel.
inlets.label: aftertouch

inlets.doc: Pitch bend, coarse byte, 64 at rest. The fine byte is sent as 0.
inlets.label: bend

inlets.doc: Channel for the messages that follow. Stores only; starts at 1.
inlets.label: channel

inlets.doc: Byte values passed straight to the outlet, as a list or one at a time. A value outside 0-255 is dropped; a list is cut at 128 bytes.
inlets.label: raw

.midiformat.name: .midiformat

outlets.doc: One message per list, such as 144 60 100: a note-on for middle C, velocity 100, channel 1.
outlets.label: midi

.midiin.description: Raw MIDI input. Every byte received on a MIDI input port leaves the outlet as an int, in arrival order and uninterpreted.
.midiin.name: .midiin

outlets.doc: Each received byte as an int. Status bytes keep their value on the wire (144-159 is a note-on, 240 starts a system-exclusive dump); data bytes are 0-127.
outlets.label: byte

params.doc: MIDI input port to listen to, counted from 0; .midiinfo lists them. A port that cannot be opened leaves the object silent, and the patch still loads.
params.name: port

.midiinfo.description: Lists the machine's MIDI ports. A bang sends the number of ports, then an index and a name for each, so a patch can find a device by name.

inlets.doc: A bang sends the listing. "input" and "output" switch which ports are listed; "refresh" scans the machine again and sends the listing when the scan is done.
inlets.label: bang

.midiinfo.name: .midiinfo

outlets.doc: The port's name, spaces included, cut at 63 characters. Sent after its index.
outlets.label: name

outlets.doc: The port's index: the port argument .midiout, .notein and the other MIDI objects take. Counted from 0.
outlets.label: index

outlets.doc: How many ports there are. Sent first; 0 when there are none.
outlets.label: count

params.doc: Which ports to list: "input" or "output". Anything else means "input".
params.name: direction

.midiout.description: Sends MIDI messages to an output port. Each list on the inlet is one message, as byte values or as built by the MIDI sender objects; a few words send common channel-mode messages.

inlets.doc: One MIDI message: a list of byte values such as 144 60 100, or a message from a sender object such as .noteon. Messages that arrive before the port is open, including the first, are dropped.
inlets.label: midi

.midiout.name: .midiout

params.doc: MIDI output port, counted from 0; .midiinfo lists them.
params.name: port

.midiparse.description: Splits a raw MIDI byte stream into notes, controllers, program changes, pressure, pitch bend and channel. Messages it does not decode leave the rightmost outlet as bytes.

inlets.doc: MIDI bytes, one int at a time or as a list of byte values. A value outside 0-255 is ignored.
inlets.label: midi

.midiparse.name: .midiparse

outlets.doc: Note as "pitch velocity"; a release reports velocity 0.
outlets.label: note

outlets.doc: Polyphonic key pressure as "pitch pressure".
outlets.label: poly

outlets.doc: Control change as "controller value".
outlets.label: control

outlets.doc: Program change, numbered from 1.
outlets.label: program

outlets.doc: Channel pressure: one value for the whole channel.
outlets.label: aftertouch

outlets.doc: Pitch bend, coarse byte only, 64 at rest.
outlets.label: bend

outlets.doc: The channel the message arrived on. Sent before the typed outlet.
outlets.label: channel

outlets.doc: Every other message as a list of byte values: system exclusive, song position, time code, clock and the rest.
outlets.label: raw

.minimum.description: Sends the smaller of a number and a stored value. The right inlet sets the stored value; a list sends its smallest item.

inlets.doc: Number: send the smaller of it and the stored value. Bang: send the last result again. List: send its smallest item, and store the second smallest.
inlets.label: in

inlets.doc: Value to compare with, stored without sending.
inlets.label: compare

.minimum.name: .minimum

outlets.doc: The smaller of the input and the stored value.
outlets.label: out

params.doc: Starting value to compare with, and what a bang sends before the first result.
params.name: initial

.mpeconfig.description: Builds the MPE configuration message that tells a device how many member channels an MPE zone uses. A value on the inlet sends it.

inlets.doc: Number of member channels; sends the message. 0 switches MPE off on the device.
inlets.label: members

.mpeconfig.name: .mpeconfig

outlets.doc: Three control-change messages on the zone's master channel, as byte lists for .midiout.
outlets.label: midi

params.doc: 0 for the lower zone (master channel 1, members counting up from 2) or 1 for the upper zone (master channel 16, members counting down from 15). Anything other than 1 means the lower zone.
params.name: zone

.mpeformat.description: Builds MPE messages: notes, per-note pitch bend, pressure and slide, on the member channel set by the right inlet. The inverse of .mpeparse.

inlets.doc: "pitch velocity"; a bare pitch sends velocity 0, a release. Sends a note-on.
inlets.label: note

inlets.doc: Per-note pitch bend, 8192 at rest, at the full 14 bits.
inlets.label: bend

inlets.doc: Per-note pressure, sent as channel pressure.
inlets.label: pressure

inlets.doc: Per-note slide, sent as controller 74.
inlets.label: slide

inlets.doc: Member channel for the messages that follow. Stores only; starts at 1.
inlets.label: channel

.mpeformat.name: .mpeformat

outlets.doc: One message per list, such as 146 60 100: a note-on for middle C on channel 3.
outlets.label: midi

.mpeparse.description: Reads an MPE MIDI stream and reports notes, per-note pitch bend, pressure and slide, each with its channel and the channel's role in the zone.

inlets.doc: MIDI bytes, one int at a time or as a list of byte values. A value outside 0-255 is ignored.
inlets.label: midi

.mpeparse.name: .mpeparse

outlets.doc: Note as "pitch velocity"; a release reports velocity 0.
outlets.label: note

outlets.doc: Pitch bend at the full 14 bits, 8192 at rest.
outlets.label: bend

outlets.doc: Channel pressure: on a member channel, that note's pressure.
outlets.label: pressure

outlets.doc: Controller 74.
outlets.label: slide

outlets.doc: The channel the message arrived on: in MPE, the note it belongs to.
outlets.label: channel

outlets.doc: The channel's role: 2 master, 1 member, 0 outside the zone. Sent first.
outlets.label: role

params.doc: 0 for the lower zone (master channel 1, members counting up from 2) or 1 for the upper zone (master channel 16, members counting down from 15). Anything other than 1 means the lower zone.
